entries.english: (Co-)plaintiff/applicant/intervenor: Rudolf von Hürnheim zu Jettenhofen, princely-bishop's councillor and steward at Eichstätt, administrator at Obermässing. (Co-)defendant/intervenor: Elector Friedrich III von der Pfalz, his governor and councillors at Amberg, and Georg Thomas von Wildenstein and Hans Hertl, the Palatine Schultheiß and judge at Neumarkt. The dispute concerns a mandate and citation involving six subjects at Griesbach and Obernried, and the right to levy taxes on Hürnheim subjects. In 1561 the Palatine government first levied the land tax; Rudolf refused to pay, whereupon judge Hertl imprisoned six of his subjects. The Elector disputes Rudolf's imperial immediacy and claims territorial and criminal jurisdiction; Rudolf asserts his exemption as a member of the Franconian Imperial Knights, Altmühl canton, and his rights over Jettenhofen and associated properties. The Imperial Chamber Court ruled on 27 January 1585 that the defendant must not interfere with Rudolf's right to levy taxes or disturb his tax exemption. The file includes proceedings from 1562–1615, especially 1571–1578, witness testimony before an imperial commission, fief charters, agreements, purchase contracts, the Rosenberg brothers' register (1530), notices of Franconian Imperial Knights' days, and documents on boundaries, high jurisdiction, tax rights, and the forest ban. A 1530 purchase contract between Konrad and Philipp von Rosenberg, brothers, and the von Hürnheim brothers concerns Jettenhofen Castle and its associated goods and rents. Registry note: process began in 1562.
